title: Staying over and getting around
title_target: ຢູ່ໂຮງແຮມ ແລະ ເດີນທາງ — Yùu hoong-héem lae dòen-tháang
goal: Book a room, complain about facilities that don't work, buy a bus or train ticket, and handle things at the border — the unit that lets you travel on your own anywhere in Laos.

complaining with ໃຊ້ບໍ່ໄດ້ and ເພ

dialogs.title: ບົດສົນທະນາ — Checking in at a guesthouse, Luang Prabang
dialogs.intro: Budi arrives at a small guesthouse. Notice that almost all of his questions use patterns you've already learned — *ມີ…ບໍ່*, *…ໄດ້ບໍ່*, *…ເທົ່າໃດ*.

lines.text: [ສະບາຍດີ|Sa-baai-dii] [ຂ້ອຍ|Khàwy][ຈອງ|jawng][ຫ້ອງ|hàwng][ໄວ້|wâi][ແລ້ວ|lèeo] [ຊື່|Sʉ̂ʉ][ບູດີ|Buu-dii]

lines.text: [ສະບາຍດີ|Sa-baai-dii][ເຈົ້າ|jâo] [ຂໍ|Khǎw][ໜັງສືຜ່ານແດນ|nǎng-sʉ̌ʉ-phàan-deen][ແດ່|dèe] [ພັກ|Phak][ຈັກ|ják][ຄືນ|khʉ́ʉn]

lines.literal: three — hundred-thousand — kip — per — night. include — food — morning — already.

lines.speaker: ບູດີ:
lines.text: [ດີ|Dii] [ມີ|Míi][ໄວໄຟ|wái-fái][ບໍ່|bàw] [ແລ້ວ|Lèeo][ນ້ຳ|nâm][ຮ້ອນ|hâwn][ມີ|míi][ບໍ່|bàw]

lines.text: [ມີ|Míi][ທັງ|tháng][ສອງ|sǎwng][ຢ່າງ|yàang] [ລະຫັດ|La-hát][ໄວໄຟ|wái-fái][ຢູ່|yùu][ເທິງ|thóeng][ໂຕະ|tó] [ອາຫານ|Aa-hǎan][ເຊົ້າ|sâo][ແຕ່|tèe][ເຈັດ|jét][ຫາ|hǎa][ເກົ້າ|kào][ໂມງ|móong]

lines.speaker: ບູດີ:
lines.text: [ຂອບໃຈ|Khàwp-jai][ຫຼາຍໆ|lǎai-lǎai][ເດີ້|dòe]

notes: **ຄືນລະ khʉ́ʉn la = "per night", and ຕໍ່ຄືນ taw khʉ́ʉn means the same.** The first is more casual, the second a bit more formal and often written on price lists. Remember the *ລະ la* pattern from unit 14: *ຄົນລະ* (per person), *ມື້ລະ* (per day).

**ໜັງສືຜ່ານແດນ nǎng-sʉ̌ʉ-phàan-deen = "passport", literally "document for crossing the border".** It's long, and people often shorten it to *ພາສປໍ pháat-saw-páw* from English. Both are understood; forms always use the long one.
**ລວມ lúam = "included, combined".** *ລວມອາຫານເຊົ້າແລ້ວ* (breakfast included), *ລວມພາສີ* (tax included), *ບໍ່ລວມ* (not included). It's the word you must ask about before agreeing to any price.
**ທັງສອງຢ່າງ tháng sǎwng yàang = "both".** The word *ທັງ tháng* means "whole, all": *ທັງໝົດ* (everything), *ທັງມື້* (all day), *ທັງໂຕ* (whole body).
**ອອກ àwk = "leave, depart", ຮອດ hâwt = "arrive".** *ລົດອອກແປດໂມງ* (the bus leaves at eight), *ຮອດບ່າຍສອງໂມງ* (arrives at two in the afternoon). To ask about schedules: *ອອກຈັກໂມງ* and *ຮອດຈັກໂມງ*.
**ແຕ່… ຫາ… tèe… hǎa… = "from… to…".** *ແຕ່ເຈັດຫາເກົ້າໂມງ* (from seven to nine). ⚠️ Here *ແຕ່ tèe* means "from", not "but" — and the only thing that tells them apart is the *ຫາ* that follows.

**ສຳລັບ sǎm-lap = "for".** *ສຳລັບມື້ຮື* (for the day after tomorrow), *ສຳລັບສອງຄົນ* (for two people). The difference from *ເພື່ອ phʉ̂a* (for, in order to) in unit 16: *ສຳລັບ* marks who or what something is for, *ເພື່ອ* marks a purpose.
**ຂໍ້ khàw = the classifier for questions and points.** *ຖາມອີກຂໍ້ໜຶ່ງ* (ask one more thing), *ຂໍ້ສອງ* (point two). The same word appears in *ຂໍ້ຄວາມ* (message) and *ຂໍ້ມູນ* (data).

**About staying in Laos.** Guesthouses are required to record your passport details and report them; that's why they ask for it up front. You can ask for it back once it's copied — the sentence is *ຂໍໜັງສືຜ່ານແດນຄືນແດ່ໄດ້ບໍ່*. Keep a digital copy yourself, because losing your passport in Laos means a trip to your embassy in Vientiane.

after: The most useful complaint phrase: **…ໃຊ້ບໍ່ໄດ້ *…sâi bàw dâi*** (…doesn't work). *ເຄື່ອງແອໃຊ້ບໍ່ໄດ້* (the AC doesn't work), *ໄວໄຟໃຊ້ບໍ່ໄດ້* (the Wi-Fi isn't working), *ນ້ຳຮ້ອນບໍ່ອອກ* (no hot water coming out). For something broken, the word is *ເພ phée*: *ປະຕູເພ* (the door is broken).

after: **ບ່ອນ *bàwn*** means "place, spot": *ບ່ອນນັ່ງ* (seat), *ບ່ອນນອນ* (place to sleep, berth), *ບ່ອນນີ້* (this spot). It's a little more concrete than *ທີ່ thìi*, which also means place.

blocks.text: Notice that **every complaint opens with *ຂໍໂທດ khǎw-thôot* and closes with *ໄດ້ບໍ່ dâi bàw***. In Laos, a complaint made as a request almost always gets fixed; a complaint made as a demand often ends with a polite smile and no change at all. It isn't about the words, it's about the manner.

blocks.text: Citizens of ASEAN countries — Budi included — can enter Laos **without a visa** for short visits, and many other nationalities can get a visa on arrival or an e-visa — but the rules change from time to time, so check before you go. What doesn't change: your passport must be valid for at least six months.

Useful phrases at a bank or exchange booth: *ຂໍແລກເງິນແດ່ khǎw lèek ngóen dèe* (I'd like to change money) and *ອັດຕາແລກປ່ຽນມື້ນີ້ເທົ່າໃດ át-taa lèek-pìan mʉ̂ʉ-nîi thao-dai* (what's today's exchange rate). Most foreign currencies are hard to exchange; bring US dollars or Thai baht.
